headline: Trump steps into Spain's big moment

sources.title: Trump loomed over the World Cup, up until the awkward trophy ceremony
Donald Trump refuses to leave World Cup trophy ceremony as Spain celebrate
President Trump steals part of spotlight as Spain celebrates World Cup title
Trump booed at World Cup as he presents Spain FIFA trophy, then lingers for lifting ceremony (video, USA TODAY)

chunks.text: On July 19, 2026, Spain won the World Cup, beating Argentina 1-0 in the final. After the game, the President of the United States, Donald Trump, walked onto the [[field]] to {{hand over}} the [[trophy]]. He was joined by Gianni Infantino, [[the head of]] FIFA, the group that {{puts on}} the World Cup. Around the world, millions of people {{tuned in}} to watch the winning team [[lift the cup]].

verbs.wrong: To shake hands with the winners
verbs.why: Officials hand over trophies at award shows, and workers hand over keys on their last day. President Trump walked onto the field to hand over the World Cup trophy to Spain.

verbs.wrong: To compete in a big contest
verbs.why: Cities put on fireworks shows, and schools put on a play each spring. FIFA is the organization that puts on the World Cup every four years.

verbs.correct: To watch a show on TV
verbs.wrong: To increase the sound of a TV
verbs.why: Viewers tune in for a season finale, and sports fans tune in for a big game. Millions of people around the world tuned in to watch the World Cup final.

chunks.text: Usually, leaders {{step aside}} after the trophy is given, so the winners can enjoy the [[moment]] [[on their own]]. But this time, President Trump {{hung around}} as the Spanish players [[celebrated]]. The team {{carried on}} cheering and dancing, with the president still standing [[close by]]. [[In the end]], Infantino had to {{step in}} and [[gently]] guide him to the side of the [[stage]].

verbs.correct: To leave space for someone else
verbs.wrong: To lead a team off the field
verbs.why: A manager can step aside for a coworker to lead a meeting, and an older leader sometimes steps aside for someone younger. Leaders usually step aside once a trophy ceremony begins, letting the winners have their moment.
Friends hang around after class, and fans sometimes hang around outside a stadium after the game. President Trump hung around on the field while the Spanish players kept celebrating.

verbs.wrong: To lift a teammate up high
verbs.why: A conversation can carry on for hours, and a celebration can carry on despite an interruption. The Spanish team carried on cheering and dancing even with the president still nearby.
A manager steps in when a shift is short staffed, and a calm friend steps in during an argument. FIFA's Gianni Infantino had to step in and guide the president to the side of the stage.

chunks.text: Not everyone was [[pleased]] to see the president on the field. Earlier, during the [[national anthems]], some fans in the [[crowd]] had {{let out}} loud [[boos]]. It was not the first time he had {{turned up}} at a [[major]] final. A year before, he had done the same thing at another trophy [[ceremony]], and fans quickly {{brought up}} that earlier moment online.

verbs.wrong: To wave a flag in the air
verbs.why: A crowd can let out a loud cheer, and a tired worker can let out a deep sigh. During the national anthems, some fans in the crowd let out loud boos.
Uninvited guests sometimes turn up at a party, and rain can turn up right before an outdoor event. It was not the first time President Trump had turned up at a major sports final.
Friends bring up old memories at a reunion, and reporters bring up a politician's past mistakes. Fans quickly brought up his earlier appearance at another trophy ceremony a year before.

chunks.text: In the end, though, the day [[belonged]] to Spain. The players {{held up}} the [[shining]] golden trophy while red and yellow [[flags]] [[waved]] across the [[stadium]]. [[Back home]], thousands of fans {{poured out}} into the [[streets]] to celebrate. For the Spanish team, nothing was going to {{take away from}} their special night, [[no matter]] who else was standing on the stage.

verbs.wrong: To carry the cup off the field
verbs.why: Winners hold up a trophy for photos, and protesters hold up signs at a rally. The Spanish players held up the golden trophy as flags waved across the stadium.

verbs.wrong: To sing songs in the street
verbs.why: Fans pour out of a stadium after a big win, and shoppers pour out of a mall during a sale. Back in Spain, thousands of fans poured out into the streets to celebrate.

verbs.correct: To make something seem less good
verbs.wrong: To end the night too soon
verbs.why: A small mistake can take away from a great performance, and rain can take away from an outdoor party. Nothing was going to take away from Spain's celebration, no matter who stood on the stage.

mainIdea.s: The US president handed the World Cup trophy to Spain but did not step aside once the ceremony began. FIFA's head had to step in and guide him away so the players could celebrate alone.
mainIdea.why: The US president hung around while the Spanish players celebrated, so FIFA's head had to step in and gently guide him to the side. Fans had also booed him earlier during the national anthems.

mainIdea.s: The US president handed the trophy to Spain's players and lingered on the field during their celebration. FIFA's head chose not to step in, and the ceremony continued as usual until it ended.
mainIdea.why: Close, but FIFA's head did have to step in. He guided the president to the side of the stage during the celebration.

mainIdea.s: Earlier this year, the president attended a golf event and presented the winning trophy to the top player there. Organizers said the short ceremony went smoothly and ended within minutes.
mainIdea.why: This describes a different ceremony at a golf event, not the World Cup final. The real story is about the US president lingering on the field after Spain's win.

tf.s: President Trump walked onto the field to hand over the World Cup trophy to Spain.

tf.s: Infantino had to step in and guide the president to the side of the stage.
tf.why: Trump hung around during the celebration, so Infantino had to step in and gently guide him to the side.

tf.s: During the anthems, the fans in the crowd cheered loudly for the president.
tf.why: During the national anthems, some fans in the crowd had let out loud boos, not cheers.

tf.s: It was the first time the president had ever turned up at a major final.
tf.why: It was not the first time he had turned up at a major final; he had done the same a year before.

tf.s: After the win, thousands of Spanish fans poured out into the streets to celebrate.
tf.why: Back home, thousands of fans poured out into the streets to celebrate Spain's victory.

tf.s: Spain's players gave the trophy back and left the stage without celebrating.
tf.why: The players held up the trophy and carried on celebrating; they did not leave without celebrating.
